steps.say: Let us learn this again with a new picture. Think of a restaurant. You are the customer. You read the menu and order a dosa. You do not enter the kitchen.
The menu is the interface. It tells you what you can ask for. It does not cook anything by itself.

board.title: Interface
board.body: The set of actions an object can do. It defines the actions but does not actually perform them.

steps.say: The kitchen is the implementation. The cook follows the steps and really makes the dosa. This is where the work happens.

board.title: Implementation
board.body: Carries out the actions defined in the interface.

steps.say: Now a textbook example. A tube light or bulb has a switch. Anything that behaves like a bulb must have turn on and turn off functions. That list of functions is the interface. How the bulb actually glows is the implementation.

board.title: Bulb: turn_on() and turn_off() are the interface

steps.say: Another worked example is the car. The driver presses the accelerator and asks for speed 70. The accelerator is the interface between the driver and the engine. The engine burns fuel and makes power. That is the implementation, and it is hidden from the driver.

board.title: Car example
board.body:
flowchart TD
A["Driver"] --> B["Accelerator: speed(70)"]
B --> C["Engine does the work"]

steps.say: For the board exam, remember this. The interface defines what can be done. The implementation does it. They are kept separate. This is a favourite two mark question, so you can do it!

board.title: Exam: Interface only defines actions; Implementation performs them

practice.question: In the restaurant analogy, which one is the interface?
practice.explanation: The menu tells what you can order, like an interface. The kitchen and cook do the real work, like the implementation.

practice.question: In the car example, what is the interface and what is the implementation?
practice.answer: The accelerator is the interface between the driver and the engine. The engine doing the actual work is the implementation.
practice.explanation: The driver uses only the accelerator. The engine's internal working is hidden and is the implementation.

steps.say: Let us go slowly now. Two words matter here. Interface and implementation. Let us understand each in simple words.
Step one. An interface is a list of things an object can do. It only says what. It does not do the work.

board.title: Interface = list of what can be done

steps.say: Step two. Implementation is the real work. It follows the instructions given in the interface.
Here is a school analogy. The school timetable says which subject is in which period. That is like the interface. The teacher actually teaching in the class is the implementation.

Now the code example from the book. The function min takes three values x, y and z, and gives the smallest. A person who calls min only needs to know its name and inputs. The if conditions inside are the implementation.

board.title: min function
board.body:
let min x y z :=
 if x < y then
  if x < z then x else z
 else
  if y < z then y else z

steps.say: Common mistakes. First, do not say the interface does the work. It does not. Second, do not mix them up. The interface is the what, and the implementation is the how.

board.title: Interface does NOT do the work

practice.question: Which statement is correct?
options: Implementation carries out the actions defined in the interface
Interface carries out the actions and implementation only lists them
Both are exactly the same thing
Interface is the hidden inner working of an object
practice.answer: Implementation carries out the actions defined in the interface
practice.explanation: The interface only defines the actions. The implementation really performs them.

practice.question: Using the school timetable analogy, explain interface and implementation in one or two sentences.
practice.answer: The timetable only lists what happens in each period, so it is the interface. The teacher actually teaching is the implementation.
practice.explanation: The timetable defines what should happen but does not teach. The teaching is the real work, which is the implementation.

steps.say: Let us start from the very basics. You already know how to use a mobile phone. You use it without knowing its circuits. Keep this in mind.
On a phone you tap the call button. The button is what you use. This is like an interface.
Inside, circuits and software connect the call. You do not see this. This is like the implementation.
The same idea comes from the textbook. A bulb has a switch. Pressing it makes the bulb glow. You need not know how it glows.

board.title: Switch = interface; how it glows = implementation

steps.say: So remember one line. Interface tells what can be done. Implementation does it. Well done, you can get this right!

board.title: Interface vs Implementation
board.body: Interface defines actions. Implementation performs them.

practice.question: A bulb has turn_on() and turn_off() functions. What are these functions called together?
practice.explanation: The list of actions an object can do is its interface. How the bulb actually glows is the implementation.

practice.question: On a phone, which part is the interface and which is the implementation?
practice.answer: The call button you tap is the interface. The hidden circuits and software that connect the call are the implementation.
practice.explanation: The user only uses the button. The inner working that does the job is the implementation.
